newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan stocks drop too far, Sakakibara tells daily.
newsitem.headline: Japan stocks drop too far, Sakakibara tells daily.

text.p: Tokyo's ailing stock market has "gone a bit too far", Eisuke Sakakibara, director of the International Finance Bureau of the Japanese Ministry of Finance said in a interview with a Japanese daily published on Tuesday.

Sakakibara, dubbed "Mr Yen" by the media for his efforts to halt the Japanese currency's rise last year, criticised commentators who have linked the recent poor performance of the Tokyo bourse to pessimism about financial deregulation in Japan.

"I do think that people are reacting quite superficially when they talk about being disappointed with the reform stance of the Hashimoto administration," he said in an interview carried with the Mainichi Daily News.

"He (Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto) says that he will implement structural reform by the year 2001, so the argument that stock prices are falling because structural reform can't be implemented is a pretext," Sakakibara was quoted as saying.
"(The market's) real intention is probably to get politics and government to foot the bill," he said without elaborating.
Markets were closed on Tuesday for a national holiday.

Tokyo stocks closed higher on Monday as the yen's weakness against the dollar eased worries that a rebound in the yen after the weekend Group of Seven (G7) meeting might pull down major export-oriented issues, brokers said.
Such issues have recently acted as a prop for the market.
The key 225-share Nikkei average gained 314.13 points or 1.76 percent to close at 18,181.17.
